question: Can the low-order expansion of an invariant-learning objective around a predictive-mode onset forecast which features appear, shrink, disappear, or become unstable as regularization increases, and can that forecast extend from a solvable bilinear model to coupled modes and nonlinear networks?

key_findings.claim: Near a simple continuous onset, invariant representation learning reduces to a Landau free energy whose effective quadratic and quartic coefficients play structurally different roles.
key_findings.evidence: Eliminating noncritical parameters gives an even scalar objective F_eff(q)=F_0+r q^2/2+u q^4/4+O(q^6). A positive effective R2 correction changes the mass r and therefore the onset; an R4 correction changes the stiffness u and therefore the amplitude after onset. The appendix proves the corresponding soft-mode reduction for a finite smooth network with a one-dimensional Hessian kernel.

key_findings.claim: In the canonical bilinear squared-loss model, an R2 control removes a predictive mode at a finite, exactly calculable strength, whereas a pure R4 control only attenuates a mode at finite strength.
key_findings.evidence: The exact reduced objective has a nonzero stable branch iff a^2>mu(mu+lambda_2 gamma), giving lambda_2,c=(a^2/mu-mu)/gamma. Its realized loading is [|a|-sqrt(mu(mu+lambda_2 gamma))]_+/(m+lambda_4 gamma): lambda_2 can zero the numerator, while lambda_4 only enlarges the denominator when the quartic coefficient remains positive.

key_findings.claim: Selective shortcut removal is possible only when the shortcut and stable directions have distinct critical strengths; environmental association by itself does not define the retained predictor.
key_findings.evidence: If lambda_2,c(shortcut)<lambda_2,c(stable), every regularization strength between the two boundaries suppresses the shortcut while preserving the stable mode. In the multifactor extension, the onset is instead controlled by the largest eigenvalue of mu^{-1} C^T(mu I+lambda_2 Gamma_E)^{-1}C, so an invariant predictor can be a combination of individually environment-sensitive coordinates.

key_findings.claim: The paper derives a method-by-method local taxonomy rather than treating invariant penalties as interchangeable.
key_findings.evidence: At the controlled reference state, MMD-mean is gate-block R2; covariance-only CORAL and Fishr are R4-leading; full CORAL combines both; IRMv1 begins at joint order four; V-REx is R4-leading only under equal null risks; IGA has a positive-semidefinite matrix R2 term plus signed higher orders; GroupDRO reweights the task potential; and Fish/MLDG has sign-indefinite quadratic and quartic corrections that can lose local stability at finite strength.

key_findings.claim: Controlled bilinear experiments closely recover the predicted onsets and distinguish finite-threshold from gradual-suppression paths.
key_findings.evidence: Across the onset probes in Figure 2, analytic and measured zero crossings differ by at most 4.7e-6. Loading curves use coefficients derived from each objective rather than fit to the trained paths, and Figure 4's theory-blind two-stage extrapolation places explicit R2, R2+R4, MMD-mean, full CORAL, and matched IGA critical strengths near the theoretical diagonal.

key_findings.claim: The qualitative objective signatures persist in small ReLU multilayer perceptrons, but depth changes the strength scale and the large-regularization tails.
key_findings.evidence: One- and two-hidden-layer width-32 ReLU models preserve the contrast between R2-like finite-strength shortcut control and quartic-dominant continuous suppression. The transition interval shifts and broadens at greater depth, and higher-order effects appear as residual loading, rebound, or nonmonotone tails rather than following the local polynomial globally.

key_findings.claim: A coupled environmental-sensitivity matrix can preserve a compensating stable pair that coordinatewise regularization destroys.
key_findings.evidence: In a three-feature construction, diagonal R2 and R4 suppress the two environment-sensitive coordinates even though their sum cancels the environmental background. Matrix R2/R4 built from the oracle Gamma_E leaves the compensated direction in its null space, suppresses the independent shortcut, and improves OOD AUC; matrix R4 additionally penalizes leakage in realized predictor space.

method.core_idea: Treat the loading of a predictive feature or collective feature direction as an order parameter, expand each invariant objective around the point where that mode becomes soft, and use the resulting low-order coefficient signature to predict the entire qualitative regularization path.
method.mechanism: The analysis first eliminates noncritical parameters by an implicit-function/Schur-complement reduction. In a canonical factorized predictor beta=w theta, squared risk plus weight decay and explicit environment-sensitive quadratic and quartic penalties yields an exactly solvable one-dimensional objective. Its mass, stiffness, critical strength, equilibrium loading, and critical exponent are derived in closed form. The same local expansion is then performed for ERM, IRM, V-REx, GroupDRO, IGA, Fish/MLDG, Fishr, Mixup, MMD, CORAL, and a profiled DANN surrogate. A matrix extension uses an environmental-sensitivity operator to identify collective soft modes. Population onset probes, full-batch finite-sample bilinear paths, width-32 ReLU paths, and a compensating-feature construction test the predictions.
assumptions: The transition of interest is local, continuous, and governed by a simple one-dimensional soft mode with all transverse Hessian directions positive after quotienting exact parameter symmetries.

The objective is sufficiently smooth and has the simultaneous sign-reversal symmetry needed for an even Landau expansion; the ReLU transfer is therefore empirical rather than covered globally by the theorem.
The canonical closed forms assume a bilinear parameterization, squared loss, positive quadratic curvature, and positive quartic stiffness; BCE shares only the local normal form.

Identifiable low-dimensional predictive modes are supplied by the controlled data construction, so feature discovery, optimizer selection, and architecture-induced entanglement are deliberately separated from objective effects.

The oracle environmental-sensitivity matrix Gamma_E is known in the coupled-mode experiment, although the authors state it is not identifiable from finite observational environments without extra structural or causal assumptions.

Early deterministic gradient-flow growth around a small perturbation is a valid diagnostic of the equilibrium Hessian zero crossing; it is not asserted to model global finite-step Adam or SGD dynamics.

techniques.role: Eliminates stable parameter directions and expresses the objective locally in the coordinate whose Hessian eigenvalue crosses zero.
Classifies algorithms by their projected quadratic, quartic, and higher-order corrections rather than by their names or intended invariance principle.
Uses strict convexity in the auxiliary factor to obtain exact phase boundaries and realized feature loadings for the canonical model.
Measures onset through the sign change of the fastest local growth rate, which equals the static mass boundary under gradient flow.
Uses a Schur complement and the spectrum of the environmental-sensitivity matrix to find compensating feature combinations.
Tracks shortcut loading, stable retention, IID/OOD AUC, and instability over strength rather than reporting one selected hyperparameter.
Brackets disappearance from empirical loading, refines the bracket, and bootstraps a local root without using the theoretical critical value to choose the fit.

evaluations.setting: Population single-shortcut onset probes over mean shift and matched correlation heterogeneity
evaluations.metric: Displacement of the early-growth zero crossing relative to ERM
evaluations.result: The analytic Landau onset and numerical measurement differ by at most 4.7e-6.
evaluations.baseline: ERM and objectives without an independent quadratic correction

evaluations.setting: Single-feature bilinear predictor, four environments, 256 or 1,024 samples per environment, five seeds
evaluations.metric: Final predictive loading across environmental-probe strength
evaluations.result: Objective-derived quartic or sextic equilibrium curves track trained paths for explicit controls and several invariant objectives without fitting coefficients to those paths.

evaluations.setting: 52 theory-blind critical-strength settings across explicit R2, R2+R4, MMD-mean, CORAL-full, and matched IGA
evaluations.metric: Empirically extrapolated strength where final loading reaches its floor
evaluations.result: Retained high-quality local fits cluster near the theoretical critical strengths; adding R4 changes branch amplitude and slope but not the shared R2 onset.

evaluations.setting: Stable-shortcut bilinear regularization paths with 256 training and 2,048 test samples per environment
evaluations.metric: Normalized stable/shortcut loading and IID/OOD AUC over regularization strength
evaluations.result: R2-like paths can enter a selective-retention interval; quartic-leading paths generally shrink continuously and retain finite-strength shortcut loading, while Fish/MLDG can become numerically unstable.
evaluations.baseline: ERM and explicit oracle R2/R4 controls

evaluations.setting: One- and two-hidden-layer ReLU MLPs of width 32 on the same stable-shortcut construction
evaluations.metric: Input-Jacobian feature loading and AUC over the regularization path
evaluations.result: The qualitative signature classes persist, but transitions broaden and move to larger nominal strengths with depth, and higher-order tails become more visible.

evaluations.setting: Three-feature compensatory-mode experiment with 1,024 training and 4,096 IID/OOD test samples per environment
evaluations.metric: Compensating-pair retention, background leakage, shortcut loading, and OOD AUC
evaluations.result: Coupled oracle-matrix controls preserve the compensated pair while suppressing shortcut and leakage; coordinate-diagonal controls destroy the pair.
evaluations.baseline: Diagonal R2/R4 and the full set of non-oracle invariant objectives

evaluations.setting: Finite-sample operator-alignment audit before training in the Figure 5 datasets
evaluations.metric: Stable versus shortcut projection of the empirical MMD/CORAL mean-matching R2 matrix
evaluations.result: Mean stable projection is 0.0286+/-0.0078 versus shortcut projection 5.092+/-0.212, explaining preservation at intermediate strength but accumulated stable suppression at very large strength.
evaluations.baseline: Oracle R2 projection 0 on the stable coordinate and 1 on the shortcut

limitations: Author-stated: the Landau polynomial is an asymptotic description near a continuous critical point, not a global model of arbitrary amplitudes or large regularization.
Author-stated: the exact critical-strength and loading formulas apply to the canonical bilinear squared-loss model; general objectives receive only local leading-order predictions.
Author-stated: the finite-network theorem requires a smooth objective and a simple soft mode; ReLU activation-boundary crossings and multidimensional critical kernels need different analysis.
Author-stated: Gamma_E is not uniquely identifiable from finitely many observational environments without a generative model, causal prior, or other structural assumptions.
Author-stated: deterministic continuous-time local gradient flow does not describe finite-step Adam/SGD, gradient noise, or global optimization trajectories.

Reviewer-identified: all quantitative validations are synthetic low-dimensional probes, and the nonlinear transfer uses only small width-32 MLPs rather than image, language, or naturally shifted benchmarks.
Reviewer-identified: the objective taxonomy is reference-state and data-distribution dependent; V-REx, Gaussian MMD, GroupDRO, and DANN explicitly lack a universal fixed order or global signature.
Reviewer-identified: the oracle coupled regularizers demonstrate a mechanism but not a deployable procedure for estimating the correct sensitivity operator from real environments.
Reviewer-identified: reporting path shape clarifies mechanism but does not establish that the predicted phenotype selects better OOD models under realistic validation constraints.
failure_modes: A discontinuous or first-order transition, multiple simultaneous soft modes, or a negative quartic coefficient invalidates the scalar continuous Landau branch used for prediction.
Higher-order terms can dominate away from onset, producing rebound, plateaus, collapse, or instability that a quadratic/quartic label cannot forecast quantitatively.
A data-estimated sensitivity matrix can be misaligned with the true stable collective mode and suppress the very predictor it is intended to retain.
Finite-sample environmental mean fluctuations create off-target R2 mass; at sufficiently large strength even an approximately aligned objective removes stable features.
Optimizer dynamics can cross activation regions, jump between metastable wells, or become numerically unstable before reaching the equilibrium branch.
Marginally stable or shortcut features with similar task-signal-to-sensitivity ratios may have no useful selective-retention window.
A coordinatewise diagnostic can miss a stable compensating combination and falsely label each constituent feature as spurious.
reusable_insights: Analyze an objective after projecting its Hessian and higher derivatives onto the actual critical mode; the presence of a monomial in raw parameters does not determine its effect.
Regularization should be evaluated as a path, because onset movement, post-onset shrinkage, plateaus, and collapse are qualitatively different behaviors hidden by one tuned point.
Finite-threshold deletion requires a positive quadratic correction along the target mode; a positive quartic term alone generally leaves residual finite-strength loading.
Stable information may occupy a low-sensitivity eigenvector of a coupled operator even when every coordinate is individually environment-sensitive.
Use explicit oracle controls as mechanism checks and separately audit how closely a practical empirical operator projects onto those oracle directions.
A theory-blind bracketing and root-estimation protocol is a useful safeguard against choosing an experimental window to agree with a known theoretical transition.
Separate exact claims for a solvable model, local asymptotic claims for related objectives, and qualitative transfer claims for deeper architectures.
open_questions: Can Gamma_E or its relevant low-sensitivity eigenspace be estimated consistently from finite environments without assuming the answer through an oracle construction?
Do objective signatures predict regularization paths in modern residual networks, transformers, and naturally shifted datasets after feature discovery and optimizer effects are restored?
How should the framework handle first-order transitions, mode degeneracy, symmetry breaking, or several interacting soft modes?
Can local coefficients be estimated online and used to choose a regularization interval before OOD labels are observed?
Which optimizer- and noise-dependent corrections turn the equilibrium Landau landscape into an accurate stochastic training-dynamics model?
Can phenotype-based objective selection improve model-selection reliability beyond ERM on DomainBed/WILDS-style benchmarks?
What causal or interventional data are minimally sufficient to distinguish a shortcut direction from a compensating stable collective mode?

competitive_landscape.title: Invariant Risk Minimization
competitive_landscape.difference: IRM introduces a representation objective whose optimal classifier agrees across environments and connects it to causal invariance. The present paper does not replace that principle; it locally expands IRMv1 and many peers to predict how their learned modes change over the regularization path.

competitive_landscape.title: Out-of-Distribution Generalization via Risk Extrapolation (REx)
competitive_landscape.difference: REx proposes worst-case risk extrapolation and the V-REx variance penalty, with causal-robustness guarantees and OOD experiments. This paper instead derives the conditions under which V-REx is quartic-leading and shows why that yields continuous shrinkage and higher-order tails rather than a universal finite deletion threshold.

competitive_landscape.title: The Risks of Invariant Risk Minimization
competitive_landscape.difference: Rosenfeld et al. give conditions under which IRM and alternatives fail to recover invariant predictors, including nonlinear counterexamples. The present analysis asks a different local mechanistic question: which mode-level phase and path phenotype follows from an objective's projected low-order terms.

competitive_landscape.title: In Search of Lost Domain Generalization
competitive_landscape.difference: DomainBed standardizes datasets, algorithms, and model-selection rules and finds carefully tuned ERM hard to beat. The current paper provides controlled synthetic mechanism tests and path predictions, but does not yet supply a DomainBed-scale empirical validation or model-selection improvement.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: the contribution is a Landau-theoretic methodology that turns projected low-order objective coefficients into predictions of onset, equilibrium loading, regularization phenotype, and coupled-mode selectivity, rather than a new invariant-learning loss. Reviewer inference after comparison: the strongest novelty is the unified path-level taxonomy plus exact canonical formulas and the spectral collective-mode extension. IRM, REx, failure analyses, and benchmark evidence all predate it; the magnetic analogy by itself is not the novelty. The claim is credible as a controlled local theory, but its practical novelty remains provisional until the signatures predict behavior in realistic architectures and natural shifts and until Gamma_E can be estimated without oracle knowledge.
reviewer_notes: Read all 33 extracted pages, including the complete method-specific expansions, proofs, finite-sample operator audit, and experimental protocol. Quantitative claims above are restricted to values printed in the text or tables. Comparisons were checked against primary arXiv records. Statements labeled reviewer inference concern external validity, identifiability, and the distinction between an organizing analogy and a deployable algorithm.
